source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Iron overload is a recognized cumulative effect of metformin and commonly produces distal paresthesias.","B":"Vitamin C toxicity is expected after prolonged metformin use because the drug increases vitamin C absorption.","C":"Vitamin B12 deficiency should be considered during long-term metformin therapy, particularly with compatible hematologic or neurologic findings.","D":"Folate excess is the characteristic nutritional complication responsible for neuropathy during metformin therapy."}}
source_row.rationale: Metformin labeling recognizes decreased vitamin B12 concentrations during treatment and recommends periodic hematologic monitoring, with vitamin B12 assessment when clinically indicated. Fatigue and paresthesias are compatible with B12 deficiency and warrant evaluation.
source_row.source_detail: Warnings and Precautions §5.2 — Vitamin B12 Deficiency. Revised 07/2026, version 8; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A client has taken metformin for several years and now reports fatigue and new distal paresthesias. Which long-term adverse effect should be considered?
